author: Epiphanius of Salamis
occasion: Epiphanius provides a summary of the contents of his larger work against heresies, indicating how many heresies are treated in each book and volume.
argument: Epiphanius states that he will show in this summary how many of the eighty heresies are in the first book, the second, and the third. He explains that the first book contains three volumes and forty-six heresies, with these names: Barbarism, Scythianism, Hellenism, Judaism, and Samaritanism. The second book contains two volumes and twenty-three heresies. The third book contains two volumes and eleven heresies. He then states that the first volume of the first book contains twenty heresies, which are as follows: Barbarism, Scythianism, Hellenism, Judaism, but the list breaks off after four items.

outline.move: Epiphanius announces his summary of the eighty heresies and gives the distribution of heresies across the three books and their volumes, beginning the list with the first volume of the first book.
